agree.reason: The 20-mile gap in 14 counties, the offer to share invoices and the concrete ask tied to July 1 give a skeptical benefits director something to check and act on, though she gets no dollar figure to weigh.

honest.reason: The letter drops the unsupported 'a third will close' claim and says plainly that it can't attribute the nine closures to rates, but 'one of our biggest groups of customers every day' slightly embellishes the 22% figure.

works_the_facts.reason: It repeats the $1.80 and 22% figures without deriving anything from them, leaving out the 3,100 prescriptions and the roughly $5,580 a year that Reilly Drug alone loses on them.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the status quo accurately: two pharmacies ready to stop filling for plan members, nine closures in two years, and members in 14 counties facing a 20-mile drive or going without.

qualification.reason: The hedge on the closures is honest and the May 1 and July 1 dates can be checked, but the warning that two pharmacies will stop filling has no date and no checkable trigger beyond 'if the rates stay the same'.

objections.reason: It answers 'members have plenty of chains' directly with the 14 counties and the 20-mile distance, and it meets 'they complain every year' indirectly by offering invoices, but it never says outright why this year is different.

fit.reason: It is a one-page open letter signed on behalf of the Alliance, which suits both the plan and the newspapers.
